description: The hand-verified expected result for the negative Joern fixture whose findings[2] carries no rule identifier at all. Every value was derived by reading the fixture against the authored contracts in harness/lib/normalize/ -- emit.FIELDS for the field set and its order, paths.REJECT_CLASSES for the class name, the adapter's documented five-step classification order for the step each record is decided at, and severity.py's no-vocabulary path for the severity triple -- and every path was resolved by hand under the documented indexing scheme against a source index measured over the pinned tree. The adapter was run afterwards to corroborate, never to source these values. Where this file and harness/lib/normalize/adapters/joern.py disagree, the disagreement is the finding: diagnose it rather than overwriting this file to match. The key names are the ones expected/reject-sarif-unresolvable-path.rows.json established and expected/reject-joern-unresolvable-path.rows.json carried into this adapter -- the shared metadata keys, the three parts rows / row_derivations / rejections, and the negative-only additions routing, rejection_boundary, rejections and counts.parse_status -- so one generic loader reads every expected file in this folder.
scanner_class_authority: AAP 0.5.4's class table fixes sast for opengrep, semgrep, datadog-static-analyzer and joern. The value is fixed in advance rather than derived from what the artifact turns out to contain, and it is identical on every row. Trivy is the single tool whose scanner_class varies by record, and joern is not it.
artifact_shape_note: This is the only artifact whose shape is the harness's own collector output rather than a tool-native format. There is no Joern output format to look up: harness/bin/run-joern.sh loads the code-property graph with importCpg, runs the bounded query set baked into harness/lib/joern-scan.sc, and that script writes the artifact itself.
condition_under_test: missing_rule_id -- a finding from which no rule identifier can be obtained by any route the shape offers. It is the rejection condition AAP 0.5.4 names 'a missing rule identifier', and this is the Joern adapter's instance of it.

fixture.shape: the collector shape the specification documents
fixture.defective_finding_members_note: Six keys rather than seven. The rule_id member is absent outright -- not present-and-null, not present-and-empty -- which is the branch of the condition where the adapter reports that no member of the shape's identifier candidate list is present at all. The null and empty-string branches are different sub-reasons of the same class and are named under rule_identifier_resolution.branches_of_this_condition.
fixture.derivation: A negative fixture is derived from captured output rather than being an excerpt of it, so the provenance is stated as a derivation. Two things are derived and nothing else is invented. First, the shape: every record is written in the documented collector shape -- rule_id rather than query_id, class_file rather than class, start_line rather than line, the severity label dropped, and the collector's own path and path_resolution members supplied. Second, findings[2] has its rule_id member removed, which is the one thing this fixture exists to assert. Nothing else about that record is disturbed: its message, its coordinate, its method signature, its line and its collector path are all left as they were, so the record is defective in exactly one way.
fixture.captured_provenance: Established per record by exhaustive search of harness/artifacts/raw/joern.json rather than asserted for the fixture as a whole, because the four records do not share one provenance. Two are re-spellings of records that artifact carries and two are not, and saying so is cheaper than a reader discovering it. The recorded sha256 above is what makes a later edit to the fixture visible: these values are re-derived when the fixture changes, never adjusted to keep a test green.

per_record_provenance.evidence: Searched all 692 findings of harness/artifacts/raw/joern.json for the substrings 'deploy.master.Master' and 'receiveAndReply' in the class and method members: zero hits. The reason is structural rather than a defect -- this provisioning's baked query set is the six queries joern-process-exec, joern-unsafe-deserialization, joern-reflection-forname, joern-message-digest, joern-cipher-getinstance and joern-xml-factory, and none of them is an rpc-handler reachability query, so no record of this kind could appear.
per_record_provenance.verified_against: the pinned tree instead: the coordinate, the enclosing method and the line are checked against the file itself under row_derivations.

per_record_provenance.evidence: harness/artifacts/raw/joern.json carries the class org.apache.spark.deploy.worker.ProcessBuilderLike$$anon$3 with the method org.apache.spark.deploy.worker.ProcessBuilderLike$$anon$3.start:java.lang.Process() at line 276 -- the same coordinate, the same method signature and the same line this record carries -- twice, under query_id joern-process-exec, with the message 'external process launch reachable in bytecode' byte-identical to this record's.
per_record_provenance.verified_against: the pinned tree as well, under row_derivations.

per_record_provenance.evidence: Searched all 692 findings for the substring 'OneForOneBlockPusher' in the class and method members: zero hits. Structural again -- the baked deserialization query matches a different call shape than a per-call-site decode of a network-supplied buffer -- so this record is the fixture's own documented-shape record. Its coordinate, its method signature and its line are nevertheless verified against the pinned tree, which is what makes the claim that only its identifier is wrong checkable rather than asserted.
per_record_provenance.verified_against: the pinned tree under rejection_boundary.attribution_is_to_the_identifier_alone, where each of the four steps it would otherwise pass is checked individually.

per_record_provenance.evidence: harness/artifacts/raw/joern.json carries the class org.apache.spark.network.yarn.YarnShuffleService with the method org.apache.spark.network.yarn.YarnShuffleService.newMergedShuffleFileManagerInstance:org.apache.spark.network.shuffle.MergedShuffleFileManager(org.apache.spark.network.util.TransportConf,java.io.File) at line 359 -- same coordinate, same signature, same line -- twice, under query_id joern-reflection-forname, with the message 'reflective class loading (Class.forName)' byte-identical to this record's.
per_record_provenance.verified_against: the pinned tree as well, under row_derivations.

fixture.why_the_documented_shape_is_the_right_ca: The positive fixture joern.json is in this provisioning's shape, so the documented shape's rule_id, class_file, start_line, path and path_resolution members and its flat cpg_* envelope are unexercised there. Carrying the documented shape here covers that half at no extra cost, and it is the only shape in which this condition can be posed at all: the identifier member whose absence is under test is the documented shape's rule_id, and the adapter's candidate list reads rule_id before query_id.
fixture.excerpt_note: The fixture is never edited to suit these rows; these rows are re-derived when the fixture changes.

routing.detected_by: normalize.shape -- SARIF is a version of "2.1.0" together with a runs array, and this document carries neither, so it is a native artifact routed by the runner that wrote it
routing.routing_decision: normalize.shape.route("joern", doc) returns tool "joern", shape "native", adapter "joern", scanner_class "sast"
routing.not_a_shape_failure: No shape-detection failure is expected here, and a test asserting one against this fixture would be asserting the wrong thing. The enclosing document is a well-formed native Joern artifact and routes cleanly; exactly one finding inside it is defective, and the adapter rejects that finding while still emitting the others. The fixtures that own shape-detection failure are near-sarif-version-only.json, near-sarif-runs-only.json and unknown-shape.json.
routing.negative_routing_test: The mandated negative routing assertion -- that a native artifact must not route to the SARIF adapter -- belongs to test_shape_routing_negative.py. A Joern artifact is a native artifact, so it is eligible material for that assertion, but the assertion itself is not this file's and is not made here.
routing.caller_fault_is_not_a_rejection: normalize.adapters.joern.JoernAdapterError describes a defective call -- the wrong tool identifier, a relative root, another tool's path base, a path base whose kind is not bytecode_class, or a document that is not an object -- and stops the caller. None of those is in play here, and none is ever counted as a rejection: a caller fault absorbed into a rejection count would let a wrong root produce a plausible dataset for a whole tool.

rule_identifier_resolution.contract: AAP 0.5.4: rule_id <- the query identifier. The identifier is the one the finding itself names, through a member of the finding. Nothing else in the document is an identifier source.

routes_the_adapter_has.note: the documented shape's member, and the first candidate of normalize.adapters.joern.RULE_ID_FIELDS

this provisioning's member, and the second candidate. The candidate list is tested for presence rather than truthiness, so a member present with an unusable value reaches the step that names why it is unusable instead of being answered by the other shape's member.

rule_identifier_resolution.there_is_no_third_route: The candidate list is exactly those two members, and both are members of the finding. The adapter reads no identifier from the envelope, from a sibling finding, or from anywhere else in the document, and the count of routes is what makes the defective record's outcome determinate rather than a matter of how hard an implementation tries.

routes_attempted_on_the_defective_record.outcome: the member is absent; the record's keys are exactly message, path, start_line, method_full_name, class_file and path_resolution
the member is absent too, so the other shape's spelling supplies nothing either

rule_identifier_resolution.branches_of_this_condition: The class covers four sub-reasons and the detail distinguishes them: no candidate member present at all, which is this record's; a candidate present and null; a candidate present and empty or whitespace only; and a candidate present but not a string. The last of those is still missing_rule_id rather than malformed_record, because the record names no query either way. This fixture exercises the first branch only, and the sub-reason is quoted under rejections.expected_detail so a test can tell the four apart.

the_substitute_that_is_sitting_right_the.statement: This adapter is the one case in the tree where a missing identifier has a plausible substitute inside the same document. The envelope carries a populated queries[] array of five entries, each an object of the form {id, count}, and those id values are identifiers of exactly the kind rule_id holds -- the same five literals, spelled the same way. An implementation could therefore 'repair' findings[2] by matching it against a queries[] entry, and the result would look like a lookup rather than a guess.
the_substitute_that_is_sitting_right_the.why_it_is_forbidden: The queries[] array records what each query RETURNED as a count. It records nothing about which finding came from which query: there is no per-finding query reference, no ordering guarantee tying findings[] to queries[], and no index. A match against it is therefore inference dressed as a lookup, which is exactly what AAP 0.1.3 rules out -- where a record cannot be attributed with certainty it is rejected and the rejection recorded as a class with its count, never guessed into a field.
the_substitute_that_is_sitting_right_the.and_the_arithmetic_proves_the_array_is_n: Measured rather than argued. The five tallies are 55, 178, 412, 23 and 24, summing to 692, while findings[] holds 4 records. 692 is the whole scan's finding count in harness/artifacts/raw/joern.json, whose six provisioned tallies are 55, 178, 412, 23, 11 and 13 -- and the documented shape's fifth tally of 24 is that shape's last two collapsed, 11 + 13. So queries[] here describes an entire scan of 692 findings while findings[] carries four records drawn from it. An array describing 692 records cannot attribute any one of four, and no arithmetic over it can.
the_substitute_that_is_sitting_right_the.the_fixture_keeps_it_populated_deliberat: Trimming queries[] to an empty array would make the assertion below hollow: an implementation cannot be shown to refuse a substitute that is not there. The array is left populated, with five entries, so the temptation is real and refusing it is a behaviour rather than a vacuity.

forbidden_substitution_sources.queries_id: The sharpest of the four, for the reason above. Two of the five declared ids are named as witnesses below precisely because a substitution from this array is the failure mode that would otherwise be invisible.
forbidden_substitution_sources.message: findings[2].message reads 'remote response deserialized into a typed message at this call site'. A keyword match on it lands on joern.java-deserialization-site, which is a real entry in this document's queries[] array -- so a message-based synthesis produces a value that passes any membership check and is wrong on principle. The message is a description of a call site, not an identifier, and it is emitted into the message field and nowhere else.
forbidden_substitution_sources.method_full_name: findings[2].method_full_name is the enclosing method's signature, an onSuccess override taking a ByteBuffer. It is carried into the rejection's identity as diagnosable context and into no dataset field, and no part of it is ever read as an identifier.
forbidden_substitution_sources.class_file: findings[2].class_file is the bytecode coordinate the path is resolved from. It answers where, never which query, and deriving an identifier from a class name would attribute a finding to a query on the strength of what the code does.
forbidden_substitution_sources.path_resolution: The collector's own explanation of how it resolved the class. It is diagnostic metadata about the collector, it reaches no dataset field at all, and it is not identifier-shaped in any case.
forbidden_substitution_sources.the_general_rule: None of these four is a route the adapter has. They are listed because each is a route an implementation could invent, and a rejection condition is only as strong as the substitutes it refuses.

rule_identifier_resolution.central_assertion: No emitted rule_id was taken from any queries[].id. Every rule_id in the rows below is the value of its own finding's rule_id member, and the rejected record contributes no identifier of any kind.
rule_identifier_resolution.why_a_value_inequality_test_would_be_hol: All three surviving identifiers are themselves declared in queries[] -- joern.rpc-handler-reaches-process-launch, joern.process-launch-site and joern.reflective-class-load each appear there as an id. A test asserting that no row's rule_id occurs anywhere in queries[] would therefore fail against a correct implementation. The assertion has to be framed on provenance and on the entries a substitution could introduce, which is what the mechanical form below does.

assertion_in_mechanical_form.statement: For each emitted row i, rows[i].rule_id is byte-equal to findings[j].rule_id for that row's own finding index j -- the surviving indices are 0, 1 and 3, in that order. This is the check that carries the assertion: it fixes each identifier to the member of the record it came from.

Neither of the two queries[].id values that no finding names appears in any row's rule_id. Those two are joern.java-deserialization-site and joern.weak-hash-algorithm. They are the only values a substitution from queries[] could introduce that are not already legitimate, so their absence is what distinguishes a correct implementation from a repairing one.

assertion_in_mechanical_form.check: no synthesis from the other members
assertion_in_mechanical_form.statement: No row's rule_id equals, contains or is contained in any findings[].message, findings[].method_full_name or findings[].class_file value in the document. Checked by substring comparison in both directions across all four findings, not by inspection.

rows is 3 and rejections is 1, not 4 and 0. Stated last and deliberately not relied on: an implementation could repair the identifier and still reject the record for some other reason, so the count alone does not settle it. The three checks above do.

witness_identifiers.note: The five declared ids are the five collector literals, so every surviving row's identifier is one of them -- which is a property of this collector's vocabulary and not evidence of where the value came from. The two witnesses are the difference between the declared set and the named set, and they must appear nowhere in the rows array.

rule_identifier_resolution.the_identifier_this_record_would_have_ca: Worth stating plainly, because a reader can reach it and the pipeline may not. A human comparing this fixture with expected/reject-joern-unresolvable-path.rows.json will see that its row 1 carries the same coordinate and the same line under the identifier joern.java-deserialization-site, and will conclude that this record 'should' carry that too. That conclusion is a human reading of two documents, and it is precisely the reading the adapter is forbidden to perform: that other document names its own identifier and this one does not, so there it is a row and here it is a counted rejection. Nothing in this file supplies the value, not even as a comment on what it would have been, and the witness check above asserts it appears in no row.
rule_identifier_resolution.why_this_adapter_is_the_hard_case: In every other adapter this condition is posed against a document that offers no substitute. A SARIF result with no ruleId and an out-of-range ruleIndex reaches no rule object at all; a Gitleaks element with no RuleID has nothing rule-shaped beside it; a Trivy record missing its section identifier has none either. Here five identifiers of exactly the right kind sit in the same document one lookup away, in the same vocabulary the field expects. The substitute is not merely conceivable, it is present -- which is what makes refusing it a behaviour worth testing rather than an accident of the fixture being thin.

field_order_authority: harness/lib/normalize/emit.py, the FIELDS constant, which harness/lib/normalize/adapters/joern.py restates as its own FIELDS because AAP 0.6.4 permits an adapter to import paths and severity and nothing else. The two were compared and are identical. Every row below carries all twelve keys in that order, present-with-null rather than omitted.
absence_convention: Absence is JSON null here and in findings.json, and an empty field in findings.csv. tool, scanner_class, rule_id, message, severity_norm, path and in_scope are never absent -- exactly emit.REQUIRED_FIELDS. rule_id in particular is a required field, which is the whole reason this fixture's defective record is a counted rejection rather than a row with a null identifier.

allowlist.note: in_scope is decided by that file alone. The globs are not copied here: the allowlist is the single authority and stays byte-exact. The glob each row matched is recorded per row under row_derivations.

shape_divergence.summary: This fixture is written in the collector shape the specification documents, which is the opposite half of the divergence expected/joern.rows.json records: that fixture captures this provisioning's shape. The divergence itself is recorded, not repaired -- AAP 0.1.3's authority rule -- and the adapter reads both shapes in a fixed field precedence so the choice is reproducible. Five members differ from the provisioned shape, and each changes a value below.
shape_divergence.documented_shape: {tool, cpg_path, generated_at, cpg_methods, cpg_typedecls, source_index_size, declaration_index_size, queries: [{id, count}], findings: [{rule_id, message, path, start_line, method_full_name, class_file, path_resolution}]}
shape_divergence.provisioned_shape: {tool, tool_version, cpg, graph: {methods, type_declarations, files}, query_set, queries: [{id, bound, returned, bound_reached, elapsed_ms, callee_prefixes[]}], findings: [{query_id, severity, message, callee, class, method, file, line}]}

differences.documented: findings[].rule_id, one of five joern. prefixed literals
differences.observed_here: findings[].rule_id on three of four records, and absent on findings[2]
differences.consequence: rule_id_from_rule_id counts 3 -- one per record that reached and passed the identifier step -- and rule_id_from_query_id counts 0. The count is 3 rather than 4 because the defective record is rejected at that step, before the provenance counter is bumped; the sibling fixture whose record fails at the path step counts 4 there instead.

differences.documented: findings[].class_file, a class-file path such as org/apache/spark/deploy/master/Master.class
differences.observed_here: findings[].class_file on every record; no class member is present
differences.consequence: coordinate_from_class_file counts 3 and coordinate_from_class counts 0. The runner metadata names class as record_path_field, so the adapter tries it first and falls through to class_file, which is why a document in either shape resolves. normalize.paths.class_key accepts either form, so the precedence decides which member is read, never how it is interpreted. Again 3 rather than 4: the coordinate step is step 4 and the defective record never reaches it.

differences.observed_here: no severity member at all -- the literal string severity does not occur anywhere in the fixture
differences.consequence: Every surviving row carries severity_native null and severity_norm Info on the no_vocabulary basis, so severity_absent counts 3 and severity_from_record_label counts 0.
differences.why_this_is_the_contract: AAP 0.5.4 places joern under 'No vocabulary at all (gitleaks; joern unless a query defines one) -- severity_native absent, severity_norm Info, the absence stated rather than a level assumed'. Here no query defines one, so the absence is stated. Info is never written by the adapter directly: severity.py owns the vocabulary, the precedence and the bands, so this file cannot disagree with severity-map.md.

differences.documented: findings[].path, the collector's own already-root-relative answer, and findings[].path_resolution, its explanation of how it got there
differences.observed_here: both present on every record, including the defective one, and non-null throughout
differences.consequence: The three surviving records each carry a collector path identical to this run's own unique resolution, so collector_path_corroborated counts 3 while collector_path_used and collector_path_disagreed both count 0. collector_explanation_present counts 3 rather than 4, because that tally is taken after the message step and the defective record is rejected before it.

differences.documented: flat cpg_methods, cpg_typedecls, source_index_size and declaration_index_size
differences.observed_here: all four present; no nested graph object
differences.consequence: envelope_graph_methods, envelope_graph_type_declarations, envelope_collector_source_index_size and envelope_collector_declaration_index_size all carry figures, while envelope_graph_files stays 0 because the nested object that would supply it is absent. The per-query tally is spelled count here rather than returned, and neither is summed into any published figure.

count_unit.per_query_tally_member: queries[].count in this shape; queries[].returned in the provisioned shape
count_unit.which_one_is_the_raw_count: len(findings) = 4. The sum of the per-query tallies is 692, and it is not the raw count and is not published as one.
count_unit.why_they_differ: The fixture carries four findings beside a queries[] array whose tallies describe a whole scan -- 692 records, which is exactly the finding count of harness/artifacts/raw/joern.json. The two numbers therefore differ by construction, and by a factor of 173, which is what makes the reconciliation assertion non-vacuous: an implementation that counted the per-query tallies instead of the findings would produce 692 against 3 rows and 1 rejection and fail loudly rather than agree silently.
count_unit.no_query_to_finding_link: No rule_id is ever taken from a queries[].id. The documented queries[] carries only {id, count} and records no link between a query and a finding: no per-finding query reference, no ordering guarantee and no index. Each finding names its own query through its own rule_id member, and the one record here that does not is rejected rather than matched. rule_identifier_resolution states this at length, because this fixture is the one that turns on it.
count_unit.authority: AAP 0.5.4 makes findings[] the reconciliation unit, and normalize.reconcile.count_records walks that same unit without building rows. The adapter deliberately publishes no count of the findings it walked, so the left-hand side of the identity cannot be taken from the traversal that builds the right-hand side.

resolution_context.path_base_source: harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json, the joern entry's path_base -- read as input, never assumed
resolution_context.why_no_filesystem_base_exists: The runner queries a graph the frontend built over staged JARs rather than over the source tree, so a reported file member is by construction the frontend's extraction path for a .class member and can never be a path in the Spark tree. The metadata therefore records a null base value rather than inventing a plausible one, and the class coordinate is the only resolvable one. Because has_explicit_base is false, no metadata-backed fallback is available to this tool at all.
resolution_context.resolution_procedure: The class coordinate is reduced by normalize.paths.class_key to <package path>/<outer type name>, truncating the basename at its first $ so a companion object, an anonymous class and a nested class all collapse to the outer type. That key is then looked up in a source index over src/main and src/test under the pinned root, across two key schemes: by_filename on <package dir>/<file base name>, and by_decl on <package dir>/<declared type name>. The union of candidates must be exactly one distinct path.
resolution_context.every_coordinate_here_resolves_uniquely: Measured over the pinned tree, all four coordinates -- including the defective record's -- have exactly one candidate. That is deliberate: it is what makes the rejection attributable to the identifier alone, and it is the property that separates this fixture from expected/reject-joern-unresolvable-path.rows.json, where the defective record's key has zero candidates.
resolution_context.declaration_scheme_is_not_optional: One of the three surviving rows resolves on the declaration scheme alone: no file is named ProcessBuilderLike.scala, and DriverRunner.scala is the file that declares the type. A filename-only index would lose that row silently, and a silently lost row is indistinguishable from a class with nothing to report.
resolution_context.gap_1_closed: The index spans src/main and src/test rather than src/main alone. Every -tests artifact the build emitted is in the graph input, so a finding can legitimately name bytecode compiled from a test tree, and such a resolution is retained with in_scope false rather than dropped. No record in this fixture resolves into a test tree, so rows_from_src_test is 0 here.
resolution_context.gap_2_closed: A resolution is taken only where the union of candidates is exactly one distinct path. Two or more is ambiguous_source_resolution with every competing candidate named, never a first-wins pick. Closing gap 1 increases ambiguity, which is why closing gap 2 is mandatory rather than optional.
resolution_context.collector_path_precedence: Fixed by the adapter. This run's own unique class-to-source resolution governs; an ambiguous key is never overridden by the collector's answer; where this run resolves nothing and the collector did supply a root-relative path, that path is emitted as-is and marked uncorroborated; and where both resolve and differ, this run's answer is kept and the disagreement recorded. All three surviving records take the first branch with the collector agreeing, so collector_path_used and collector_path_disagreed are both 0. The defective record's collector path is never consulted at all -- the rejection happens two steps earlier.
resolution_context.root_dependence: These rows depend on a live tree: the class-to-source resolution reads the pinned checkout at $SPARK_SRC. Every emitted path is expressed relative to that root and none is absolute, and no absolute path appears anywhere in this file.
resolution_context.severity_source: No record states a severity, and this shape has no rule object to fall back on, so every row takes severity.py's no-vocabulary path: severity_native null, severity_norm Info, basis no_vocabulary. The absence is stated rather than a level assumed.
resolution_context.package_coordinate: null on every row. A Joern finding names a bytecode call site rather than a package, and this shape supplies no coordinate to carry. The absence is explicitly not a rejection: the unformable_package_coordinate class covers a dependency-oriented record, and this shape is not one.

rejection_boundary.statement: A missing rule identifier is a rejection. It is not a row with a null rule_id, not a row with a substituted identifier, and not a dropped record. The three alternatives each hide the record or assert something the artifact does not state; counting it under a named class keeps it visible and keeps the arithmetic honest.
rejection_boundary.why_it_can_only_be_a_rejection: rule_id is one of emit.REQUIRED_FIELDS -- the seven are tool, scanner_class, rule_id, message, severity_norm, path and in_scope -- and emit.OPTIONAL_FIELDS is exactly severity_native, start_line, cwe, cve and package_coordinate, which AAP 0.8.2 fixes as the only five absence is permitted for. emit.py refuses an empty or null required field rather than writing one, so a record with no obtainable identifier has no valid twelve-field row representation at all.

not_a_rejection.case: an identifier present, non-empty and outside the known set -- a value no query this run pinned declares
not_a_rejection.expected: a kept row carrying that identifier verbatim
not_a_rejection.evidence: The adapter validates the identifier's presence and type, never its membership in KNOWN_RULE_IDS. AAP 0.4.2 has the baked query set read from the runner, so an unlisted identifier is a legitimate finding from a set that constant predates, and dropping it would silently shrink the tool's count.

not_a_rejection.case: a record with no severity member
not_a_rejection.expected: a kept row with severity_native null and severity_norm Info
not_a_rejection.evidence: severity_native is one of the five fields absence is permitted for, and severity_norm is never absent. This is the ordinary case for this tool in this shape.

not_a_rejection.case: a resolution into a src/test tree, or outside the twelve authoritative globs
not_a_rejection.expected: a kept row with in_scope false, counted under rows_out_of_scope and, for the test tree, rows_from_src_test
not_a_rejection.evidence: AAP 0.5.4 requires a test-JAR finding kept out of scope rather than dropped, and AAP 0.9.3 repeats it among the recorded-not-halting conditions. Out of scope means kept and marked, never rejected.

not_a_rejection.case: a record with no start_line at all
not_a_rejection.expected: a kept row with start_line null, counted under start_line_absent
not_a_rejection.evidence: Only a start_line that is present and unusable is the non_integer_start_line condition, which reject-joern-non-integer-start-line.json owns.

rejection_boundary.defective_record_reaches_no_identifier: Verified from the fixture rather than assumed. findings[2] has exactly the keys message, path, start_line, method_full_name, class_file and path_resolution: there is no rule_id member and no query_id member, so both routes the adapter has are exhausted on their first read, and no third reading of the record exists.
rejection_boundary.attribution_is_to_the_identifier_alone: Asserted, not assumed, because the assertion this file carries is on the rejection class and a record defective in two ways could be counted under either while a test that merely counted rejections still passed. Every other property of findings[2] was hand-checked against the fixture and the pinned tree and is sound. Step 1 would pass: the findings element is a JSON object. Step 3 would pass: message is present and non-empty.
